newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha static, near-term spreads widen.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha static, near-term spreads widen.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha prices were little changed on Wednesday, while the backwardation in near-term spreads strengthened after several end-users scouted the market on Tuesday for May cargoes, traders said.
The one-month spread from first-half May was indicated at plus $2.00/3.00 after having been traded at $2.50 on Tuesday. It was discussed at $1.00/2.00 late last week.

One of the firms that probed the market on Tuesday bought one second-half May cargo at about $1.75 over the mean of Japanese quotes for its petrochemical affiliate. On Monday, another second-half cargo was bought at a $1.00 premium.
First-half June/first-half July was talked at plus $2.50/3.50, a bit narrower than Tuesday's $3.00/4.00.
Open-spec naphtha for first-half June was bid at $222.50 per tonne, while offers were heard at $223.50. Second-half June was quoted $1.50 to $2.00 lower than the first-half June level.

Jet kerosene and gas oil trading remained lethargic due to high domestic stocks, traders said. Activity in middle distillates markets usually picks up this time of year ahead of spring turnarounds at refineries, they said.
Kerosene and gas oil stocks at the end of February were up by 33 percent and 39 percent, respectively, from a year ago.
